title: Geo-anchored dedicated pools: placement tiers, graceful contraction, and residency compliance runbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Context:
We need a prescriptive runbook and implementation plan for geo-anchored dedicated pools that balances throughput guarantees, autoscaling responsiveness, and strict data residency constraints. This ticket captures design decisions, operator playbook, API/flag surface, and verification criteria required to safely launch regional + multi-zone dedicated pools that can gracefully contract (soft-drain) and failover while honoring tenancy residency locks.

Goals:
- Define placement tiers (anchored, flexible, spillover) and their allowed movements across zones/regions.
- Specify graceful contraction semantics (soft-drain windows, cordon vs drain, KV cache preservation, in-flight request draining).
- Produce residency enforcement model for per-tenant data locality (hard locks, read-only failover exceptions, audit trails).
- Describe autoscaling policies with throughput guarantees and safety gates (min-capacity, surge buffers, rate-limited shrink).
- Provide operator runbook for zone evacuation, region failover, and partial capacity loss scenarios.
- Define metrics, SLOs, and automated remediation steps for degradations.

Design notes / decisions to make:
1) Placement tiers:
   - Anchored pools: reserved capacity pinned to a region/zone for residency-locked tenants. No automatic relocation; manual admin approval required for any movement.
   - Flexible pools: capacity prefers a home region but can be rebalanced within a regional boundary to meet utilization targets. Subject to soft-drain windows and data-locality checks.
   - Spillover pools: global spare capacity used only when local capacity is exhausted; allowed only if tenant has spillover opt-in. Spillover must be logged and short-lived.

2) Graceful contraction semantics:
   - Soft-drain window default = 5 minutes for short drains (configurable per-pool). During soft-drain, new requests are routed preferentially away; existing streaming/KV cached contexts are allowed to complete within a bounded tail.
   - Hard-evacuation only after escalation: will trigger cordon -> 30m soft-drain -> preemptive snapshot of KV cache -> live migration fallback if required.
   - Throughput guardrails: do not shrink below min-guaranteed throughput for tenants with active reservations. Shrink decisions must consult per-tenant reservation ledger.

3) Residency enforcement model:
   - Residency lock modes: HARD (no cross-region allocation), SOFT (allow read-only failover or degraded mode), OPT_IN_SPILLOVER.
   - All cross-region allocations must generate an auditable record, include customer notification (if HARD lock) and an automatic revert window (24h) unless manually approved.
   - Network and encryption requirements: traffic must remain within customer-approved cloud regions; KMS key usage must be tied to region-specific CMKs if present.

4) Autoscaling policies and throughput guarantees:
   - Autoscaler will expose two knobs: target_utilization and min_guaranteed_tps. For dedicated pools with reservations, min_guaranteed_tps cannot be auto-scaled below reservation commitments.
   - Surge capacity: maintain a configurable surge buffer (default 15% of committed capacity) to absorb spikes without violating latency SLOs. Surge buffer is replenished over a cooldown window.
   - Shrink safety: implement rate-limited shrink (max X% capacity per 10m) and require passing of safety checks (no pending soft-drains, no KV write backlog).

Acceptance criteria:
- API: create/update pool supports 'placement_tier' (anchored|flexible|spillover) and 'residency_mode' (HARD|SOFT|OPT_IN_SPILLOVER).
- Operator console shows per-pool residency lock, active soft-drains, and a history of cross-region allocations.
- Autoscaler respects min_guaranteed_tps and enforces shrink rate-limits.
- Runbook: documented steps for zone evacuation, with explicit rollback/verification commands and dashboard links.
- Chaos test: automated test that simulates a zone outage and validates that HARD-locked tenants are never placed outside their region; SOFT-locked tenants either enter degraded read-only mode or failover per policy.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- Key metrics: regional_capacity_utilization, soft_drain_in_progress, cross_region_allocations, min_tps_breaches, average_tail_latency_during_drain.
- Alerts: P0 on min_tps_breaches for paying tenants; P1 on unexpected cross-region allocations.

Rollout plan:
1) Impl feature flags: unexposed API fields behind ff/dedicated_geo_placement_v1.
2) Smoke deploy to canary customers (two internal beta tenants).
3) Run chaos test and manual evacuation drill.
4) Gradual opt-in via Console for customers with residency needs; default pools remain flexible.
5) Full enablement and docs update (console + developer docs) after 3-week validation window.

Artifacts & links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Dedicated/Geo+Anchored+Pools+Runbook
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4289 (WIP)
- Prototype dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dedicated/pools/geo-anchors

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How strict should hard locks be when region experiences catastrophic total loss (legal vs availability)? Propose policy: fail closed by default but add emergency-override policy with stronger audit and legal approval.
- Snapshotting KV caches vs letting in-flight contexts finish: snapshotting reduces migration time but may cause increased token retransmission and cost.

Next steps:
- Implement API shape and autoscaler checks (ENG).
- Draft operator runbook and add evacuation scripts (SRE).
- Security review (required) for cross-region audit trails & KMS behavior.
